title: Check a word in a sentence
description: Write a function `sentence_contains(sentence, word)` that returns whether `word` appears in `sentence`, using the `in` operator.
examples:
sentence_contains('I hope this course is not full of jargon', 'jargon')
-> True
hints: The `in` operator checks membership directly on the whole sentence string - it doesn't require splitting the sentence into individual words first.
expected_behavior: Returns True if word is a substring of sentence.

hidden_tests.call: sentence_contains('I hope this course is not full of jargon', 'jargon')
hidden_tests.label: source item 14

hidden_tests.call: sentence_contains('I hope this course is not full of jargon', 'boring')
hidden_tests.label: absent word

solution:
def sentence_contains(sentence, word):
    return word in sentence
explanation: in doesn't care whether the surrounding text is a single word or a whole sentence - it's a substring check either way.
